stage: Research-only native flow experiment; not final product implementation
question: How do positive FunctionCall deposits and multi-hop funding differ from explicit Transfer actions and principal-refund aggregation?
node: Existing reviewed isolated near-sandbox2.14.0, protocol88 if reported
fixture: Official generic rs_contract WASM sha256a2ad8d2da73576d23f3104c6c5d789569534de517678b8b3842e8668764a5082, no business guard
authority: Separate controlled owner full-access key; positive deposits cannot use the existing function-call-only agent key. All keys local/in-memory.

cases.action: Owner calls storage fixture with1NEAR deposit
cases.expected: Containing receipt commits; native deposit credited without an explicit Transfer action; storage change observable.

cases.action: Owner calls panicking fixture with1NEAR deposit
cases.expected: Call receipt fails, no receiver principal credit retained, successful1NEAR system refund to owner.

cases.action: Owner deposits1NEAR into vault call that emits1NEAR Transfer to merchant
cases.expected: Committed ingress and outgoing edge; owner's principal debit1, merchant credit1, not a2NEAR purchase.

cases.action: Owner submits one receipt batch with1NEAR Transfer and1NEAR FunctionCall deposit that panics
cases.expected: Both actions roll back; total2NEAR system balance refund to owner; no retained vault principal credit.

measurement: Raw local RPC, explicit receipt body/outcome identity and finality, before/after balances/state, parent-linked refund. Do not classify positive calls from success text only.
limits: No merchant data, live model or guard comparison.
Internal/native-edge sums are not automatically external expense totals; role/intent scope remains explicit.
Contract recipient may route money elsewhere; this experiment does not establish arbitrary-contract semantic ownership.
No external funding, accounts, payments or wallet operations.
